resources.string: Nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses, simplified coronal view
These paired air spaces lie in the forehead bone above the inner parts of the eye sockets. The two sides often differ in shape and size.
A cluster of small air spaces lies between the upper nasal cavity and the eye socket on each side. Thin bony walls separate the cells.
These large air spaces lie inside the upper jaw, beneath the eye sockets and to either side of the nasal cavity.
Air passes through the spaces around the nasal conchae. The septum separates the two sides, and the hard palate forms the floor.
These lowest curved shelves project inward from the outer walls of the nasal cavity. Their moist lining helps warm and humidify incoming air.
